# pdns_record (Resource)

Manages a single DNS record (rrset) within a PowerDNS zone.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "pdns_zone" "example_com" {
  name = "example.com."

  dnssec = false

  nameservers = [
    {
      hostname = "ns1",
      address  = "10.10.10.1"
    },
    {
      hostname = "ns2",
      address  = "10.10.10.2"
    }
  ]

  soa = {
    rname = "hostmaster"

    refresh = 10800
    retry   = 3600
    expire  = 604800
    ttl     = 3600
  }

}

resource "pdns_record" "test_aaaa" {
  zone = "example.com."

  name = "test"

  type = "AAAA"
  records = [
    "2345:425:2ca1::567:5673:23b5",
  ]
}

resource "pdns_record" "test2_a" {
  zone = pdns_zone.example_com.name

  name = "test2"

  type = "A"
  records = [
    "10.10.10.4",
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) LValue of the record (name). This value will be added as prefix to the name. Supports chaining by dot e.g. `sub.test` is a valid value.
- `records` (List of String) RValue to which the record points. For A type records this are IP Addresses. For CNAMEs this are other FQDNs and so on. The order is not significant: PowerDNS returns the records sorted and in its canonical form (e.g. AAAA addresses compressed and lowercase), and the configured values are kept as long as the server holds the same records.
- `type` (String) Type of the record in uppercase, e.g. `A`, `AAAA` or `CNAME`. Changing it replaces the record.
- `zone` (String) ID of the zone in which the record should be created. The name must end with a dot `.`.

### Optional

- `comments` (List of String) List of comments to append to the record
- `ttl` (Number) TTL of the record

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Records are imported by `<zone>/<name>/<type>`. Give `name` exactly as in the
# configuration: relative to the zone (`test`) or fully qualified
# (`test.example.com.`). The records are imported in the order and form
# PowerDNS returns them (sorted, canonical), so if the configuration lists them
# differently, the first plan shows an in-place update that only rewrites them.
terraform import pdns_record.test2_a example.com./test2/A
```
